articles.title: Home Assistant cameras gain HomeKit Secure Video recording
articles.dek: Owners opt in per camera and link a motion sensor; recording starts without footage from before the event.
body: Home Assistant adds HomeKit Secure Video recording for cameras exposed to Apple Home in accessory mode. Owners opt in for each camera and link a motion sensor, giving the home hub the signal to request a recording.

Raphael Hehl tested a UniFi Protect G4 Dome sending H.264 video: motion produced a recording in the Home app and the hub ended it normally. Turning a camera off in Apple Home also stops its live video and snapshots; changing recording or audio permissions ends an active recording.
The implementation does not yet buffer footage before recording begins. In the reported test, converting an H.265 stream took too long to satisfy the home hub, so that path remains unfinished.

pullRequests.title: Add HomeKit Secure Video recording to HomeKit cameras

articles.title: Music Assistant curbs requests that can block a music account
articles.dek: Artist playback favors your library and top tracks, while service waits no longer mark songs unavailable.
body: Music Assistant stops expanding a single artist selection into requests for an entire online catalog. Artist playback defaults to music in the listener’s library, falling back to top tracks. The previous all-tracks option becomes all tracks from that artist’s albums in the library, and whole Artists, Albums and Playlists folders can no longer be played with one tap.

Large artist pages stop after 100 releases from a music service; YouTube Music keeps a separate limit for each section. SoundCloud, YouTube Music and Deezer also reduce or pace their requests. The changes address operations that could send hundreds of requests from one action and cause an account to be temporarily blocked.

When a service asks Music Assistant to wait more than a minute, playback reports that wait instead of skipping through tracks and marking them unavailable. Looking up a new selection also stops after sixty seconds if it cannot finish, freeing the player without replacing its queue or interrupting existing music.

articles.title: Home Assistant manages setup for its next voice preview
articles.dek: Labs installs the supporting app, while satellite wake-word verification still needs a separate enabling step.
body: Home Assistant brings its next-generation voice preview into Labs with an integration that installs and connects the supporting Voice app. It checks for app updates at startup and removes the managed app when the preview is disabled.

Assist can use the app to check a satellite’s wake word and detect where a command ends, retaining its existing local processing when the app is unavailable. Related Voice Preview Edition firmware can send buffered wake-word audio when Home Assistant requests it; in that mode, it waits for acceptance before lowering music volume and omits the wake sound so the command can follow immediately.

The satellite connection does not yet request that buffered audio: a separate follow-up enables those requests. Michael Hansen’s end-to-end test included that follow-up and accepted real wake words while rejecting near misses. These changes do not automatically enable the preview for existing installations.

articles.title: Try Home Assistant controls inside the documentation
articles.dek: Live examples let contributors explore cards and whole dashboards without connecting a real home.
body: Home Assistant’s contributor documentation adds interactive examples beside the controls and entity properties it explains. Readers can try a light, adjust a thermostat or explore a dashboard without setting up a Home Assistant server; the demonstrations use simulated devices in the browser.

Aidan Timson brings examples to nineteen entity pages and moves seventy-eight card demonstrations across twenty-five dashboard pages onto the same hosted demo system. New guides explain how card authors can put a card, section, view or whole dashboard on their own website, with shared state across its controls.

Timson’s November 6 explanation describes dashboard tabs and internal navigation that stay inside the example rather than changing the surrounding page’s address. The simulation has limits: the entity-page media controls, for example, do not perform normal playback actions.

articles.title: HomePods regain playback and controls through Music Assistant
articles.dek: The AirPlay sender handles newer HomePods and restores controls in Apple’s Home app.
body: Music Assistant’s AirPlay sender corrects failures that left HomePod mini 2 speakers silent or prevented buffered playback from starting on HomePods running OS 27.2. Hardware checks cover standalone and stereo-pair HomePod minis.

HomePods using the sender’s native timing connection also expose track information, artwork and play/pause through the Home app and Control Center. Testing covered a HomePod mini on OS 27.2 and a group containing a stereo pair and a single speaker. The Home app’s volume slider is not enabled by this change.

articles.title: Home Assistant apps reconnect when the screen wakes
articles.dek: An expired access session no longer leaves embedded apps waiting for the next timer tick.
body: Home Assistant refreshes an app panel’s access session as soon as the page becomes visible again. Previously, a phone or computer could sleep through the refresh timer, leaving an embedded app such as evcc unable to connect for up to a minute after waking.
Matthias verifies recovery on an iPhone in the Companion app and a Mac browser, making a first contribution to Home Assistant’s frontend.

articles.title: Squeezebox volume settings stop playing too loudly
articles.dek: Radio, Touch and Boom players use the volume curve their firmware expects.
body: Music Assistant’s Squeezebox connection library corrects volume levels on Squeezebox Radio, Touch and Boom players. They had played louder than requested, especially at low settings, and volume changes could briefly break up the sound.

The library now uses the same volume curve as Lyrion Music Server for those devices. Measurements on a Squeezebox Radio running firmware 7.7.3 matched the reference commands, and listening checks confirmed that the cuts disappeared.

articles.title: Tuya camera feeders report food levels and jams
articles.dek: Compatible feeders expose the last feeding amount and two distinct problem signals.
body: Home Assistant adds feeding readings for supported Tuya pet feeders that identify themselves as cameras. The readings show the last amount dispensed and whether the food supply is full, low or lacking.

Two problem sensors separately report blocked feeding and stuck food, giving automations a way to flag a feeder that needs attention. The addition covers the camera-feeder product identified by the existing device handler; it does not establish support for every Tuya camera or feeder.

articles.title: Home Assistant stops a repeated MQTT restart loop
articles.dek: Conflicting saved device descriptions are rejected with instructions for clearing them.
body: Home Assistant stops repeatedly restarting its MQTT device connection when two saved discovery messages identify the same entity and one belongs to a disabled device. Each message could move the entity between enabled and disabled devices, starting another restart thirty seconds later.

The first discovered identity takes precedence. Home Assistant rejects the conflicting message and names both discovery topics in the error, directing the owner to clear at least one saved message. One restart of the connection can still occur just after startup before the conflict is recognized.

pullRequests.title: Fix MQTT reload loop on duplicate unique ID of a disabled entity

articles.title: ESPHome restores missing Daly battery readings
articles.dek: Fast polling no longer prevents cell voltages and temperatures from being read.
body: ESPHome restores cell-voltage and temperature readings from Daly battery-management systems when the polling interval is shorter than a full reading cycle. A one-second interval could keep restarting the cycle before those final measurements were requested, leaving them unknown while the other readings worked.

Andreas Hergert makes the running cycle finish before another begins and advances sooner when a complete reply arrives. He verified the correction on an ESP-12E connected to a 16-cell LiFePO4 battery with a one-second update interval.

pullRequests.title: [daly_bms] Finish the request cycle before starting a new one

articles.title: Blueprint conditions can select the trigger that fired
articles.dek: The automation editor offers the blueprint’s trigger IDs instead of incorrectly reporting them missing.
body: Home Assistant lists a blueprint’s trigger IDs when a condition input asks which trigger started the automation. The picker previously showed no triggers and could mark valid IDs as missing, making these conditions confusing to configure.
The editor reads the blueprint with its inputs applied and saves the selected condition back into its input. Dan Spencer makes his first contribution to the frontend with the correction.

articles.title: Matter.js stops repeating failed firmware offers
articles.dek: Controllers using the library avoid repeated offers of an unavailable image and wait after a failed update.
body: Matter.js corrects update loops in which a controller announces a locally supplied firmware file, then tells the device that no update is available. The library uses the same selection rule for both steps: local test files are offered only when test-image support is enabled.

It also keeps permission tied to the chosen firmware version and stops repeatedly announcing an undeliverable update. A failed attempt is held back from further announcements for 24 hours unless fresh consent is given; the device can still request it itself. Applications using Matter.js need to adopt the change, and separate failures while transferring firmware remain outside this correction.

articles.title: Music Assistant offers a shorter setup for existing music apps
articles.dek: Both starting points retain every feature; the app-to-speaker path leaves library setup for later.
body: Music Assistant’s first-run setup explains that its two starting points guide setup rather than limiting features. The full experience combines services, local music and speakers, while the existing-app path concentrates on speakers and app connections.

That shorter path leaves library, network and extra-user settings for later and finishes with app-playback guidance. The wizard counts steps only after the choice is confirmed, and its recap shows the selected path.

articles.title: Aeotec power strips give each outlet its own device
articles.dek: Owners can name and assign the DSC11’s sockets separately while existing controls keep working.
body: Z-Wave JS identifies each of an Aeotec DSC11 power strip’s four outlets separately, so owners can name and assign them to rooms. Jeff Hessenflow tested two strips with Home Assistant: each gained four child devices while existing entity identifiers and switch helpers followed the same outlets. Hidden meter readings stay hidden unless explicitly made visible.

roadmapUpdates.summary: Matt Beauchamp Buck shares a HomeCore demonstration and design-call ideas for explaining settings without cluttering small screens, including a switch for help icons or a dedicated explanation view. The field-help opportunity remains in Shaping; no approach has been chosen.
